answer: A concrete defense is bridge-cost weighting: an identity's standing depends on how many independent threads of attestation tie it to the trusted core, not how many accounts vouch in a tight ring. A sybil cluster can mint thousands of nodes, but they hang off the honest graph by a few costly bridges; cut those and it falls, so auditors score the whole raven cluster as one unit. Forging real weight needs many independent bridges, each a distinct honest vouch, copper-bottomed and not self-minted. Faking N identities costs N relationships, not N keypairs.
